questions.q: What does {{ ref('stg_customers') }} actually become when dbt compiles a model?
options: The model's real, fully-qualified table name in whatever environment is currently building
A literal string, unchanged, sent to the warehouse as-is
A comment that dbt ignores at runtime
A hardcoded reference to the production schema only
questions.explain: ref() is resolved at compile time into the actual fully-qualified table name for the current build environment (dev, staging, prod, etc.).

questions.q: According to the real DAG diagram in this lesson, what two models feed into the `customers` model?
options: stg_customers and stg_orders
raw_customers and raw_orders
orders and payments
customers_v1 and customers_v2
questions.explain: The diagram shows stg_customers and stg_orders both flowing into the customers model via ref() calls.

questions.q: Why does hardcoding a real table name instead of using ref() cause problems across environments?
options: The hardcoded schema may not exist (or may be named differently) in another developer's dev environment or in production
Hardcoded table names run faster than ref() calls
dbt automatically converts hardcoded names into ref() calls, so there's no real difference
Hardcoded names are actually required for staging models specifically
questions.explain: A hardcoded schema name is often specific to one person's dev environment and won't exist as written elsewhere, including production.

questions.q: What silent problem does skipping ref() create for dbt's dependency graph?
options: dbt has no way to know the model depends on the other one, so it can't guarantee the correct build order
dbt throws an immediate, loud error and refuses to run at all
It has no effect on the dependency graph whatsoever
It automatically promotes the model to a source
questions.explain: Because the DAG is built entirely from ref()/source() calls, a hardcoded reference is invisible to dbt and can lead to models building in the wrong order without any error.

questions.q: What is the DAG (the graph shown in this lesson) built from?
options: Every ref() and source() call dbt finds across all the project's model files
A manually maintained diagram someone updates by hand
The order files appear alphabetically in the models/ folder
Data pulled live from the warehouse's query history
questions.explain: dbt derives the DAG directly from the ref()/source() calls in the project's code — it is never hand-drawn.
